evidence.claim: Flagged txn 3478782 is $292.36, 6.55x the card's 180-day mean of $44.66 and above its historical max of $121.32 (amount z = 9.8) - the only genuinely anomalous attribute.

Channel and product match the baseline perfectly: 35/35 prior transactions were online, product C (channel_share 1.0, product_share 1.0); the transaction is not on a new device or in a new region for the card.
No burst or sequence: the episode window contains exactly one transaction, with no card-testing run (<$5 authorizations) and no just-under-$500 run, so patterns 1, 2 and 3 are not supported.

The shared device profile 'Trident/7.0 | unknown | ie 11.0 for tablet | unknown' appears on 46 cards all-time (14 in window) and is this cardholder's own habitual device (8 of 35 baseline txns), so it is a common user-agent string, not a rare ring identifier; the flagged txn carries no device record at all.

Prior confirmed fraud on this same card: CC-4160, one online transaction of $90.54 on 2016-09-29, closed as card_not_present_fraud - evidence the number has been exposed before, but of a much smaller and differently-shaped episode.
Five semantically near-identical closed cases (similarity 0.80-0.81) all involved a high model score on an unusually large amount and were cleared after the cardholder confirmed the purchase.
R1 requires verification rather than a block when a single signal carries the case and probability is below 0.70.
Cardholder confirms the $292.36 purchase; under R3 the alert closes as no fraud with the confirmation recorded.

case.summary: A single $292.36 online purchase on C11891-K1 scored 0.79 because it is 6.55x the card's mean and above its all-time max. Every other attribute is in-pattern: the card is online-only, product C only, the device and region are not new, and there is no surrounding burst or testing sequence. The device-sharing links to four heavily-defrauded cards rest on a generic IE-tablet user-agent seen on 46 cards all-time that is also this cardholder's own regular device, so they do not establish a shared origin. The card does have one small prior confirmed CNP fraud (CC-4160, $90.54), which justified caution but not a block on one signal. Under R1 the initial action was VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER; the cardholder confirmed the purchase, so under R3 the case closes as no fraud, consistent with five closely analogous cleared cases.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Customer confirms they made the $292.36 online purchase on 2016-11-22 and recognises the merchant.

sar.reason: No report: activity assessed as legitimate (R3); §3a filing conditions do not apply.

stop_reason: A verification response settled the question: the cardholder confirmed the only anomalous transaction, and with no burst, no new device or region and no credible shared-origin link, further steps would not change the decision.
